title: Shared-vs-forked infrastructure table with vital-info-translations (M1)
context: PLAN v0.2 adds an M1 deliverable: a 'shared vs forked' infrastructure table with vital-info-translations so that the two projects converge on one high-stakes translation pipeline (allow-list schema, glossary schema, review workflow) rather than diverging into parallel implementations. The adjacent-opportunities section names this the 'keystone asset': the criticality-tiering, license-as-data allow-list, back-translation gate, clinician sign-off, provenance, and CI structural checks should generalize to any high-stakes multilingual content project. The working recommendation is one shared pipeline, separate deliverable repos. Open Question #11 asks: one pipeline or three repos with vital-info-translations / multilingual-signage-templates?
objective: Research the infrastructure overlap between emergency-phrasebooks and vital-info-translations, produce a shared-vs-forked comparison table, and recommend the convergence path for the high-stakes translation pipeline.
acceptanceCriteria: Table enumerates the key pipeline components (allow-list schema, glossary schema, review workflow, back-translation gate, provenance schema, CI structural checks, disclaimer enforcement) for both projects
Identifies components that are identical or near-identical in both projects and are candidates for a shared package
Identifies components that genuinely differ (scope, risk tier, content domain) and should remain project-specific
Proposes the convergence path: which components to factor into a shared package/process, which repo(s) host the shared code, how separate deliverable repos consume it
Explicitly answers Open Question #11 (one pipeline or three repos) with a reasoned recommendation
Committed as docs/shared-pipeline-infra-table.md and referenced from PLAN.md M1 section
